context.intent: Strengthen backend↔UI interaction reliability without breaking gameplay functionality.
pain_points: Monolithic Flask surface in webdash.py (~2.4k LOC) mixes routing, state orchestration, and event handling.
status.py mirrors large portions of webdash state with ad-hoc guards, making /api/status fragile.
stations/main.js (~3.3k LOC) handles rendering, polling, state management, and UI logic in one file.
Loose JSON contracts between backend and UI; schema drift causes runtime errors rather than compile-time signals.
Global mutable singletons (RADAR, CAP, RUNTIME) make it hard to reason about lifecycle and introduce race conditions.
guardrails: Preserve existing gameplay flows after each phase; no large flag-day changes.
Maintain API compatibility until explicit version bump and UI migration are ready.
Add regression harnesses before code motion to avoid repeated hotfix cycles.

phases.name: Baseline & Guardrails
objectives: Capture the current backend↔UI contract and add automated monitors so regressions are caught early.
key_actions: Extract JSON snapshots of /api/status, /radar endpoints, and CAP mission payloads; store under docs/contracts/ with dated fixtures.
Add pytest integration tests that call the real Flask app (or GameRuntime) to validate status payload shape and watchdog behaviour.
Introduce lightweight smoke CLI (bin/status_probe.py) to replicate the Stations polling loop for manual verification.
Configure watchdog thresholds and logging to emit structured events instead of stack dumps, making stalls diagnosable.
deliverables: CI rule to run the smoke probe on every build
verification: Smoke probe runs for 5 simulated minutes without watchdog resets.

phases.name: Runtime Facade & Event Bus
objectives: Isolate cross-module state access behind a typed service layer and replace ad-hoc globals with an event bus.
key_actions: Create projects/falklandV2/services/runtime_facade.py exposing read-only views for radar, cap, mission, audio.
Route all status-building code through the facade; forbid direct imports of webdash globals outside the Flask app.
Introduce a simple synchronous event bus (pub/sub) to broadcast spawn, cap, and audio events to interested modules.
Backfill unit tests that ensure facade methods return serialisable, finite values.
deliverables: services/runtime_facade.py with docstrings and type hints
migration guide documenting which modules switch to the facade
verification: Logging shows facade usage (no direct RADAR attribute access in new code).

phases.name: Typed API Contracts
objectives: Define explicit schemas for backend responses to prevent UI drift.
key_actions: Adopt Pydantic (or dataclasses + jsonschema) for status payloads, radar contacts, and CAP missions.
Generate JSON schema documents automatically as part of build (e.g., scripts/generate_schema.py).
Embed schema version and Git SHA in every payload; add server-side validation before responses leave Flask.
Add backward-compatible coercion paths so older UI clients continue working during rollout.
deliverables: Fail-fast validation middleware raising descriptive errors.
verification: Contract tests validate payloads against generated schema.
Runtime logs show zero schema validation failures during soak tests.

phases.name: Modularise Backend Endpoints
objectives: Split monolithic webdash Flask app into focused blueprints/services and remove circular imports.
key_actions: Create projects/falklandV2/api/__init__.py with Flask blueprint per domain (status, radar, cap, diagnostics).
Move watchdog utilities into projects/falklandV2/services/watchdog_service.py with clear interface.
Refactor status.py to consume the facade + schemas, returning dataclasses rather than dict assembly.
Introduce background scheduler (e.g., APScheduler or custom loop) for periodic tasks instead of sharing Flask threads.
deliverables: New api package with blueprint registration in serve.py
Refactored tests pointing at blueprint endpoints
Deprecation notes for legacy webdash helpers
verification: Flask app imports without touching heavy globals.
Integration tests continue to pass; manual UI smoke confirms endpoints unchanged.

phases.name: Frontend Modularisation
objectives: Break stations/main.js into composable modules with explicit data adapters.
key_actions: Introduce projects/falklandV2/static/src/ directory with ES modules (e.g., apiClient.js, radarView.js, capPanel.js).
Add a lightweight build step (esbuild or Rollup) producing static/stations/main.bundle.js while keeping legacy file for fallback.
Implement a central store (simple event emitter) to manage status polling and deliver updates to feature modules.
Map schema objects to view models in a dedicated adapter layer; reject incomplete payloads early with user-friendly toasts.
deliverables: Updated HTML referencing bundled assets with cache-busting hashes
verification: UI smoke scenarios (radar updates, CAP launches, audio events) run without console errors.
Bundle build succeeds on CI; linting and unit tests cover new modules.

phases.name: Interaction Resilience & Telemetry
objectives: Add observability, graceful degradation, and rollback levers once modular pieces are in place.
key_actions: Implement circuit-breaker style behaviour in the frontend polling client to show stale data warnings instead of hard stalls.
Add structured telemetry (e.g., OpenTelemetry exporters or JSON logs) for key interactions: status poll latency, schema mismatches, CAP engagement events.
Introduce feature flags to toggle new modules or schemas, enabling incremental rollout.
Document recovery procedures and add automated rollback scripts.
verification: Chaos test: simulate backend delays and verify UI shows fallback state.
Feature flags allow switching between legacy and new bundles without redeploy.

risks.description: Frontend clients that are not upgraded may reject stricter schemas.
mitigations: Announce schema versioning via release notes.

risks.description: Introducing a JS build step may complicate deployment.
mitigations: Start with esbuild single file bundle executed via simple npm script in CI.
Provide prebuilt bundle artefacts for environments lacking Node.

risks.description: Refactor spans multiple domains; availability of SMEs may slow progress.
mitigations: Run parallel spikes per phase with clear owners.
Timebox phases and merge partial wins rather than blocking on perfection.
